problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit of maintenance checks across seven critical regional facilities:

Facility Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (10,191)  
Facility Beta: Positioned at grid reference (179,155)  
Facility Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (167,126)  
Facility Delta: Positioned at grid reference (182,164)  
Facility Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (117,163)  
Facility Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (111,95)  
Facility Eta: Positioned at grid reference (137,45)  

Travel distances between facilities are predefined in kilometers:  
Alpha to Gamma: 169.9 km  
Alpha to Delta: 174.1 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 110.6 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 139.3 km  
Alpha to Eta: 193.5 km  
Beta to Gamma: 31.4 km  
Beta to Delta: 9.5 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 62.5 km  
Beta to Zeta: 90.7 km  
Beta to Eta: 117.7 km  
Gamma to Delta: 40.9 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 62.2 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 64.0 km  
Gamma to Eta: 86.4 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 65.0 km  
Delta to Zeta: 99.0 km  
Delta to Eta: 127.2 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 68.3 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 119.7 km  
Zeta to Eta: 56.4 km  

Due to infrastructural constraints, no direct route exists between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta.  
Furthermore, the routing plan must incorporate exactly one of two specified critical links: either the connection between Beta and Gamma, or the connection between Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits every facility precisely once, concluding at the point of origin.
